note: Per-row retention profiling is known (RAIDR/AVATAR); VRT makes measured deadlines unsafe without margin; MRAM writeback tier is the twist.
Close to Flikker/approximate-DRAM work; per-row decay curves and bit-significance placement are incremental; SoftMC demo easy.
DRV canary standby is known; mature-node SRAM is ~50x less dense than DRAM, so stack cannot substitute HBM capacity.
Region-graded MTJ stacks on one die are process-hostile; MRAM density lags DRAM; refresh-free on hot logic is the real benefit.
Lid magnet replacing field-free SOT layers is a twist on embedded-magnet SOT; field uniformity and cross-tier interference uncertain.
Write-verify and WER-tuned short pulses are well studied; link-level NACK adds little novelty.
Head fabs have dense TMR patterning and idle capacity; MTJ-plus-selector crosspoint margins are the key doubt.
Lock-in readout conflicts with ns access; AHE signal ~0.1% too small for dense arrays; AFM spintronics widely researched.
NEMS-switch DRAM proposals exist; relay stiction and contact wear contradict unlimited endurance; interposer density very low.
Bistable stiction NEMS memory known; KOZ placement is a niche metadata store with relay reliability doubts.
Racetrack for sequential DNN weights already proposed; domain-wall pinning variability unsolved; per-track Kerr calibration not scalable.
Live polarization-loop monitoring during bonding is a sensible process-control twist; improves yield rather than cost/bit.
Symmetric FeCaps show equal small-signal C at zero bias; needs engineered asymmetry and tens-of-aF sensing at speed.
Reusing BAW filter lines is new; AlScN high coercive field and limited endurance conflict with working-memory role.
Co-locating domain-wall memory with TFLN modulators is novel but yields only a small, low-density buffer.
SiC DRAM with hour-long retention shown in 1990s; power-device design rules give poor density.
Training save/restore exists; skipping retraining saves only a few percent idle I/O power, with drift risk.
Write-intensity-driven SRAM/STT-RAM hybrid migration is long-established art.
Plated micro-toroid core planes in substrates is a fresh revival, but substrate line widths give kb-class density.
Follows MIT/SkyWater N3XT CNFET work and known metallic-tube breakdown; stacked SRAM density still trails DRAM.
GPU temperature swings exceed the 5-8 K hysteresis window; holding state with waste heat is novel but fragile.
